title: The normalization of a scheme in a finite extension of a residue field is a normal integral scheme, integral over the base, with the extension as generic point
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $x\in X$ a point with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], $K/\kappa(x)$ a finite field extension, and $h:\operatorname{Spec}K	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)	o X$ the composite of the induced morphism with the canonical morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and there are a scheme $Y$, an integral morphism $
u:Y	o X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and a morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}K	o Y$ with $h=
u\circ g$ such that: (a) $Y$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] all of whose local rings $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ are integrally closed domains (Y is normal); (b) $g$ maps the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to the generic point $\eta_Y$ of $Y$ and induces an isomorphism $\kappa(\eta_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of fields, i.e. $g$ is the inclusion of the generic point of $Y$ with $K$ as function field. (One may take for $
u$ the normalization of $X$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, Stacks 035H: $Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal O')$ with $\mathcal O'$ the integral closure of $\mathcal O_X$ in $h_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$; if $Z\subseteq X$ is the reduced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{x\}}$, it is also the normalization of $Z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, by the last clause of Stacks 035I, which is the scheme used in the proof of Stacks 09Z6.)

Y is a normal integral scheme ... it is clear that K is the function field of Y'; the function-field identification is called clear there)
